notes:
Overview: Polaris FlowGuard builds queuing and orchestration software used by mid-to-large enterprise contact centers. Evaluating Redwood for agent-assist + ticket summarization with strict burst-resilience requirements.

Key ask: keep agent latency p99 under 300ms for short-turn responses and maintain SLA during seasonal peaks (20x baseline traffic). Must support graceful degradation (fallback to quantized model variant) and per-tenant routing for data residency.

What they told us (quotes):
- 'We cannot have agent stalls during peak promotions; callbacks must never exceed 10s.' — Director of Engineering
- 'If the model degrades we need transparent routing to a lower-cost fallback and auditing per token.' — Head of Ops

Technical constraints / preferences:
- Integration points: Zendesk, ServiceNow, proprietary IVR hooks (tool-calling from model to internal APIs).
- Target throughput: 6k concurrent agents at peak; sustained 18k qps for embeddings/rerank jobs during nightly bulk summarization windows.
- Latency targets: inference p50 <60ms, p95 <180ms, p99 <300ms for generation in agent-assist flows (short context).
- Cost sensitivity: high for embeddings and nightly summarization; looking for Optimize recommendations for batching + quantization.
- Model preferences: prefer open Llama-style variants where we can pin quantized 8-bit variants; want fallback chain (local 7B quantized -> dedicated 13B -> hosted 70B only for highest-quality syntheses).
- Reliability patterns: need automatic circuit-breaker on queue backpressure, cross-region fallback, and traffic shaping for scheduled promotions.

Security / compliance notes:
- Must integrate with customer KMS, SOC2 required, SSO/SAML for console access, retention controls for transcripts (30-365 day options), and audit logging for all model calls.

Procurement & commercial:
- Interested in Dedicated capacity contract with burst credits and private VPC control-plane. Legal asked for SLA on seasonal multipliers (ability to bump capacity 3x within 6 hours).
- Budget band indicated $250k–$1M ARR depending on included support and data residency add-ons.

Sales cues / win themes:
- Emphasize Redwood Optimize for batching & KV caching recommendations (big cost wins on nightly summarization).
- Highlight dedicated pool autoscaling and explicit burst credits for predictable behavior.
- Provide a security appendix showing KMS/HSM, retention controls, and SOC2 artifacts (we have drive doc linked).

Short-term POC plan:
- Week 0: onboarding + SAML test account (SE to stand up).
- Week 1–2: baseline run on 1x dedicated instance; measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost.
- Week 3: introduce simulated 10x and 20x spikes (load harness provided by Polaris). Validate circuit-breaker and fallback chain.
- Week 4: canary 5% production traffic, finalize SLA addendum.

Open questions for engineering:
- How quickly can Redwood pivot to a quantized local fallback per-request (milliseconds to switch)?
- Are per-tenant KV caches feasible to avoid cross-tenant contamination?
- Exact billing model for burst credits and cross-region fallback.
